iep_goals.description: When experiencing sensory overload, Marcus will independently request or use a calming strategy (e.g., noise-canceling headphones, break space) and return to task within 5 minutes in 4 of 5 opportunities.
Marcus will solve double-digit addition problems with regrouping at 80% accuracy across three consecutive probes.

speaker_turns.speaker: Teacher
speaker_turns.text: Good morning, everyone. Marcus, let's start with our math warm-up — double-digit addition on page twelve.

speaker_turns.speaker: Marcus
speaker_turns.text: Okay. I already did the first two. Thirty-seven plus twenty-eight is sixty-five.

speaker_turns.speaker: Teacher
speaker_turns.text: Nice work carrying the one. Keep going — you've got eight more on that set.

speaker_turns.speaker: Peer
speaker_turns.text: Can somebody turn the music down? It's really loud.

speaker_turns.speaker: Marcus
speaker_turns.text: It's too noisy. I need my headphones.

speaker_turns.speaker: Teacher
speaker_turns.text: Absolutely, Marcus. Grab your noise-canceling headphones from the calm shelf. Take a two-minute reset if you need it.

speaker_turns.speaker: Marcus
speaker_turns.text: I'm ready. Back to the worksheet.

speaker_turns.speaker: Teacher
speaker_turns.text: Great self-advocacy. You were back on task in under three minutes.

speaker_turns.speaker: Teacher
speaker_turns.text: Marcus, let's check your accuracy. You got seven of eight correct on the regrouping set — that's about eighty-seven percent.

speaker_turns.speaker: Marcus
speaker_turns.text: I messed up number five because I forgot to carry.

speaker_turns.speaker: Teacher
speaker_turns.text: That's okay — you caught it when we reviewed. Circle that one and try a similar problem next.

speaker_turns.speaker: Peer
speaker_turns.text: Hey Marcus, give me that eraser! Come on!

speaker_turns.speaker: Marcus
speaker_turns.text: No! Stop taking my stuff! Leave me alone!

speaker_turns.speaker: Teacher
speaker_turns.text: Marcus, take a breath with me. Peer, please return the eraser and give Marcus space. Marcus, would you like the break corner or headphones again?

speaker_turns.speaker: Marcus
speaker_turns.text: Headphones. And I want to finish my math.

speaker_turns.speaker: Teacher
speaker_turns.text: Good choice. You used your words after the first reaction. Let's reset and finish the last two problems.

speaker_turns.speaker: Teacher
speaker_turns.text: Transition time to centers. Marcus, put your worksheet in the blue folder and join reading group at table two.

speaker_turns.speaker: Marcus
speaker_turns.text: I don't want to move. The lights are buzzing and my stomach hurts.

speaker_turns.speaker: Teacher
speaker_turns.text: I hear you. Sensory check — lights are a bit bright. You can take the soft lamp seat at table two, and we'll do a short calm-down first. Timer for three minutes.

speaker_turns.speaker: Marcus
speaker_turns.text: Okay. Soft seat. I'm going.

speaker_turns.speaker: Teacher
speaker_turns.text: Wrapping up. Marcus completed his math probe above eighty percent and used headphones twice today without needing a full exit from the room. Strong morning overall.
